question: Which of the following is NOT one of the components of the Panchayati Raj institutions in India at the village level? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Gram Sabha
Gram Panchayat
Nyaya Panchayat
Panchayat Samiti
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Panchayat Samiti

Explanation:
Panchayati Raj in India has three tiers: village, intermediate, and district levels. At the village level, the main components are the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat. Nyaya Panchayat is also a village-level body for dispute resolution, though it is not mandatory. Panchayat Samiti is the intermediate-level institution (block/taluka level), thus it is not a village-level component. Hence, among the given options, 'Panchayat Samiti' is NOT a component at the village level. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj.

☛ Nyaya Panchayat → Dispute resolution body at village level
☛ Panchayat Samiti → Intermediate-level institution
☛ 73rd Amendment → Gives constitutional status to Panchayati Raj
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भारत में ग्राम स्तर पर पंचायती राज संस्थाओं का घटक नहीं है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारत में पंचायती राज व्यवस्था के तीन स्तर हैं - ग्राम स्तर, मध्यवर्ती स्तर और जिला स्तर। ग्राम स्तर पर ग्राम सभा और ग्राम पंचायत मुख्य घटक हैं। न्याय पंचायत भी ग्राम स्तर पर विवाद निपटाने का निकाय है, हालांकि यह अनिवार्य नहीं है। पंचायत समिति मध्यवर्ती स्तर (ब्लॉक/तहसील) की संस्था है, जो ग्राम स्तर पर नहीं आती। इसलिए, प्रश्न में दिए गए विकल्पों में से 'पंचायत समिति' ग्राम स्तर का घटक नहीं है। 73वें संविधान संशोधन (1992) ने पंचायती राज को संवैधानिक दर्जा दिया।

question: Why does the parliamentary system prevent executive despotism? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Because the Prime Minister has unlimited power
Because the judiciary can override executive decisions without checks
Because executive authority is dispersed among a group of ministers accountable to the Parliament
Because the military can intervene in governance
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Because executive authority is dispersed among a group of ministers accountable to the Parliament

Explanation:
In a parliamentary system, the executive power is vested in the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, which is collectively responsible to the Parliament. This distribution of power prevents any single individual from becoming despotic. The principle of collective responsibility ensures that ministers act as a team and are accountable to the legislature. If the government loses the confidence of the Parliament, it can be removed via a vote of no-confidence. Unlike a presidential system, the executive here derives its legitimacy from the legislature and remains under its constant scrutiny. Thus, the parliamentary system acts as a check on executive despotism by ensuring accountability and diffusion of power.

☛ What mechanism removes a government in a parliamentary system? → Vote of no-confidence
☛ Under which article of the Indian Constitution is the Council of Ministers mentioned? → Article 74
☛ Key feature of parliamentary system? → Collective responsibility
☛ Which country is the origin of the Westminster system? → United Kingdom

question: In which of the following cases did the court restrict the Parliament from curtailing any Fundamental Right? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala
Golaknath vs State of Punjab
A K Gopalan vs State of Madras
Indira Gandhi vs Raj Narayan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Golaknath vs State of Punjab

Explanation:
In Golaknath vs State of Punjab (1967), the Supreme Court ruled that the Parliament cannot abridge or curtail any Fundamental Right through constitutional amendments under Article 368. The Court held that the amending power is limited and cannot be used to destroy or take away fundamental rights. This decision laid the foundation for the basic structure doctrine, later clarified in Kesavananda Bharati. It emphasized the supremacy of the Preamble and fundamental rights. The Parliament responded by passing the 24th Amendment to restore its amending power over fundamental rights.

☛ Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) → Parliament cannot alter basic structure of Constitution.
☛ A.K. Gopalan case (1950) → Narrow interpretation of Article 21.
☛ Indira Gandhi vs Raj Narayan (1975) → Election dispute and emergency related case.
☛ Basic Structure Doctrine → Established in Kesavananda Bharati case.

question: How can a foreigner who has lived in India for 12 years acquire Indian citizenship? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: By registration
By naturalisation
By birth
By descent
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is By naturalisation

Explanation:
Indian citizenship can be acquired through five modes under the Citizenship Act, 1955: by birth, by descent, by registration, by naturalisation, and by incorporation of territory. A foreign national who has lived in India for 12 years can acquire citizenship through naturalisation. The applicant must fulfill conditions such as residence, good character, and language proficiency. For naturalisation, the person must have resided in India for at least 9 years out of the 12 years immediately preceding the application. This process is governed by the Third Schedule of the Citizenship Act.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What is the minimum residence period for citizenship by naturalisation? → 12 years (with 9 years immediately preceding)
☛ Is Indian father required for citizenship by birth? → Yes (for births before 1987)
☛ Who can get citizenship by registration? → Persons of Indian origin or married women
☛ Is Indian father sufficient for citizenship by descent? → Yes (for births before 1992)

question: Which of the following is the primary basis for allocating seats in the Rajya Sabha among various States and Union Territories in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Literacy rate of the population
Population of each state or union territory
Economic contribution of each state
Geographical area of each state
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Population of each state or union territory

Explanation:
The allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha is based on the Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution. The primary criterion is the population of each state or union territory. States with higher population get more seats. This system ensures equitable representation of states in the federal structure. Literacy rate, economic contribution, or geographical area are not factors for seat allocation in the Rajya Sabha.

question: Which of the following statements is true about the Permanent Lok Adalat under Section 22-B of The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: The award of the Permanent Lok Adalat is not binding on the parties.
The Permanent Lok Adalat can handle cases up to a certain monetary limit (currently ₹1 crore).
The Permanent Lok Adalat can only act as a conciliator and cannot decide disputes.
The Permanent Lok Adalat has jurisdiction over disputes related to criminal offences.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Permanent Lok Adalat can handle cases up to a certain monetary limit (currently ₹1 crore).

Explanation:
Under Section 22-B of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, the Permanent Lok Adalat is established to handle disputes related to public utility services, banking, insurance, transportation, etc. It can adjudicate cases up to a monetary limit of ₹1 crore. Its award is binding on the parties and no appeal lies against it. The Permanent Lok Adalat can act both as a conciliator and, if conciliation fails, can decide the dispute. Its jurisdiction does not extend to criminal offences.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What is the current monetary limit for cases handled by the Permanent Lok Adalat? → ₹1 crore
☛ Nature of the award of Permanent Lok Adalat? → Binding on parties and no appeal
☛ Which types of disputes are handled by the Permanent Lok Adalat? → Disputes related to public utility services, banking, insurance, etc.
☛ Does the Permanent Lok Adalat only act as a conciliator? → No, it acts as both conciliator and adjudicator

question: The Charter Act of 1833 created a separate ______. (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 2)

question: What is the term duration for representatives in municipalities in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 2)

7 years
3 years
10 years
solution:

question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution does the High Court exercise its original jurisdiction by issuing writs? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 245
Article 231
Article 226
Article 32
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 226

Explanation:
Article 226 of the Indian Constitution empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for other purposes. This original jurisdiction allows High Courts to issue orders like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari. The jurisdiction extends to the entire territory of the state or part thereof. In contrast, Article 32 provides similar writ jurisdiction to the Supreme Court. Article 231 deals with the establishment of a common High Court for two or more states. Article 245 defines the territorial limits of legislative powers of Parliament and state legislatures. The power of High Courts to issue writs under Article 226 is broader than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32, as it covers not only fundamental rights but also legal rights.

☛ Supreme Courts power to issue writs → Article 32
☛ Types of writs issued by High Courts → 5 types (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari)
☛ Article 231 related to → Common High Court for two or more states
☛ Article 245 related to → Territorial extent of laws made by Parliament and state legislatures

Minerva Mills Case (1980)
Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)
solution:

Explanation:
In this landmark judgment, the Supreme Court struck down the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2014 and the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) Act, 2014 as unconstitutional. The Court held that NJAC posed a threat to judicial independence, which is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution. It reaffirmed that the primacy of the judiciary in judicial appointments must be maintained. This verdict restored the collegium system for appointing judges. The case is a cornerstone for the principle of separation of powers and judicial appointments in India.

question: Which of the following acts of the East India Company mandated that selection for civil employees in British Indian territory would be based on the competitive examinations? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Charter Act 1793
Pitt’s India Act 1784
Charter Act 1853
Charter Act 1813
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Charter Act 1853

Explanation:
The Charter Act of 1853 mandated that selection for civil employees in British Indian territory would be based on competitive examinations. This act renewed the charter of the East India Company and ordered open competition for recruitment to the civil service. It abolished the nomination powers of the directors of the company and recommended the establishment of an independent commission for selection. Although the competitive examinations actually began in 1855, the legal basis was provided by this act. It was a significant reform in Indian administration, promoting merit and transparency. The act also separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's council by adding new members for legislation. This paved the way for a more modern and efficient bureaucracy in India.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states about a directive to states for the settlement of international disputes by arbitration? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 51c
Article 51b
Article 51d
Article 51e
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 51d

Explanation:
Article 51 of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). It deals with the promotion of international peace and security. It has four clauses: (a) promote international peace and security, (b) maintain just and honourable relations between nations, (c) foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and (d) encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration. Clause (d) specifically directs the State to settle international disputes through arbitration. Being a directive principle, it is not enforceable by any court, but it is fundamental in the governance of the country.

question: In the context of the Panchayati Raj system in India, what does the term 'Village Panchayat' refer to? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: A district-level administrative body
A block-level committee
An urban municipal corporation
Local government at the village level
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Local government at the village level

Explanation:
In the Panchayati Raj system of India, the term 'Village Panchayat' refers to the local self-government at the village level. It is the lowest tier of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system, which includes the Village Panchayat, Block Panchayat, and District Panchayat. The Village Panchayat is constituted for one or more villages, and its members are directly elected by the rural voters. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave it constitutional status. The Village Panchayat is responsible for implementing development schemes, collecting taxes, and maintaining basic services like drinking water, sanitation, and roads at the village level. It plays a crucial role in grassroots democracy and rural development.

question: In the 1892 Indian Councils Act, the British government introduced certain reforms in response to Indian demands. Which of the following was a significant provision of this Act? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Provision for Indian representation in the Imperial Legislative Council
Granting full self-governance to Indian provinces
Establishment of a separate electorate for Muslims
Introduction of direct elections for legislative councils
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Provision for Indian representation in the Imperial Legislative Council

Explanation:
The 1892 Indian Councils Act introduced reforms in response to demands from the Indian National Congress. A key provision was increasing the number of non-official members in the Imperial Legislative Council and provincial councils, though they were nominated, not elected. The Act allowed councils to discuss budgets and ask questions, but retained the principle of indirect election. Full self-governance, separate electorates (introduced in 1909), and direct elections were not part of this Act. It was passed during the tenure of Viceroy Lord Lansdowne and marked a small step towards Indian representation in governance.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India prohibits the State from discriminating against the use of wells, tanks and places of public entertainment? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 18
Article 15
Article 17
Article 16
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 15

Explanation:
Article 15(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution specifically prohibits the State from discriminating against any citizen on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth in the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads and places of public entertainment. This fundamental right falls under the Right to Equality (Articles 14–18). Article 15 deals exclusively with prohibition of discrimination, while Article 17 abolishes untouchability, Article 18 abolishes titles, and Article 14 provides equality before law. Article 16 ensures equality of opportunity in public employment. Thus, the correct answer is Article 15, not 16, 17 or 18.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states about the directive for the state to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 40
Article 37
Article 38
Article 39
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 38

Explanation:
Article 38 of the Indian Constitution directs the state to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people. It is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which guide the government in policy-making. Article 38 specifically emphasizes social, economic and political justice. It mandates the state to strive to minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities. This article is placed under Part IV of the Constitution and is non-justiciable, meaning it cannot be enforced by courts, but it is fundamental in the governance of the country. The concept of a welfare state is embodied in this directive.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India prevents any child below the age of 14 years from being employed in the factory, mine or hazardous occupation? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2)

Article 24
Article 19
solution:

Explanation:
Article 24 of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or hazardous occupations. It is part of the Right against Exploitation under Fundamental Rights. Article 21 (Right to Life) and Article 23 (Prohibition of Human Trafficking and Forced Labor) deal with different subjects. This provision protects the physical and mental development of children.

question: In October 2024, the Mediation Act, 2023 came into force. What is a key feature introduced by this legislation? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: It replaces arbitration and conciliation with mediation as the sole dispute resolution method.
It mandates that all mediation proceedings must be conducted only by retired judges.
It abolishes the role of mediators in public sector disputes.
It makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before court proceedings.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before court proceedings.

Explanation:
The Mediation Act, 2023 provides a comprehensive legal framework for mediation in India. Its key feature is the provision of pre-litigation mediation, which makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before approaching the court. This aims to reduce the burden on courts and provide speedy resolution of disputes. The Act provides for registration and certification of mediators and makes mediation agreements enforceable. However, certain disputes such as those relating to criminal or family matters are exempted. This law is a step towards making India a global mediation hub.

However, Muslims are specifically excluded from this Act, as the government argues that these are Muslim-majority nations and thus Muslims do not face religious persecution there. The CAA expedites the citizenship process for eligible migrants, reducing the residency requirement from 11 years to just 5 years. This Act has been a subject of widespread debate and legal challenges regarding its constitutional validity and secular principles.

question: Which Constitutional provision directs the State to ensure that justice is not denied to any citizen due to economic or other disabilities? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 32
Article 14
Article 21
Article 39A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 39A

Explanation:
Article 39A of the Indian Constitution directs the State to ensure that the legal system promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity and that no citizen is denied justice due to economic or other disabilities. This article is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) and emphasizes providing free legal aid to the poor and weaker sections. It was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976. While Article 32 provides the right to constitutional remedies, Article 14 guarantees equality before law, and Article 21 protects life and personal liberty, only Article 39A specifically addresses the denial of justice due to economic or other disabilities.

question: Which of the following Directive Principles is mentioned in Article 44 of the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry
Uniform civil code for the citizens
Equal justice and free legal aid
Promotion of co-operative societies
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Uniform civil code for the citizens

Explanation:
Article 44 of the Constitution of India is one of the Directive Principles of State Policy. It directs the State to endeavor to secure a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens throughout the territory of India. This provision aims to replace the personal laws based on religions with a common set of laws governing marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption. The Uniform Civil Code promotes national unity and gender equality. However, being a Directive Principle, it is not enforceable by courts. The inclusion of Article 44 reflects the vision of a secular and progressive society. Goa is the only Indian state that has a Uniform Civil Code in practice. This article is part of the socialist and secular principles of the Constitution.

question: What is the dual role of the highest judicial officer in a district? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Nyaya Panchayat head for civil cases and Gram Kutchery head for criminal cases
District Judge for civil cases and Sessions Judge for criminal cases
Chief Judicial Magistrate for civil cases and Munsiff for criminal cases
Subordinate Judge for civil cases and Metropolitan Magistrate for criminal cases
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is District Judge for civil cases and Sessions Judge for criminal cases

Explanation:
The highest judicial officer in a district is the District Judge, who plays a dual role. In civil matters, he acts as the District Judge, and in criminal matters, he acts as the Sessions Judge. This arrangement is a fundamental aspect of the Indian judiciary. The District Judge is the head of the judicial administration in the district and has the authority to preside over both civil and criminal cases. As a Sessions Judge, he hears serious criminal cases that fall under the jurisdiction of the Sessions Court. This dual role makes the District Judge the highest judicial authority in the district, ensuring efficient handling of cases across both domains. The empowerment of the District Judge under the Criminal Procedure Code and Civil Procedure Code facilitates streamlined justice delivery at the district level.
